protections: P1: an event the bridge fetches from the homeserver by an ID taken from an incoming Matrix event (reply target or edit original) must be checked to belong to the same room as the incoming event before its content is put into the outgoing IRC text or the event cache.
P2 (inferred, unverified): the bridge must not quote content that the replying sender could not see itself; today the bridge bot's own read access is used as a stand-in.

evidence: src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1041 reply target ID comes from sender-controlled content['m.relates_to']['m.in_reply_to'].event_id
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1288-1290 the bot intent calls getEvent(event.room_id, replyEventId), and the returned eventContent.room_id is never compared with event.room_id
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1301 the fetched body becomes rplSource
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1323 rplSource is cut to replySourceMaxLength (the 'truncated message content' in the advisory)
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1358-1362 it is put into the reply template sent to IRC via MatrixHandler.ts:1044

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The FIXME at MatrixHandler.ts:1055-1057 says getEvent returns the new (edited) content anyway, and only a short s/old/new/ diff is emitted, not the original body, so it looks harmless.
evidence: src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1050-1051 original event ID comes from sender-controlled m.relates_to.event_id when rel_type is m.replace
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1067-1070 getEvent(event.room_id, originalEventId) result body is used with no room_id check (bot intent, or IRC ghost intent for PMs at 1059-1062)
src/util/MessageDiff.ts:38 removed words of 'from' (the fetched body) go into substitutions
src/util/MessageDiff.ts:68 emitted as s/<original words>/<new>/ so fragments of the fetched body reach IRC

traps.reason_to_dismiss: It is only a cache write, and the lookup at 1284 is already keyed by the incoming room.
evidence: src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1304 cacheEvent(eventContent.room_id, eventContent.event_id, ...) keys the cache on room and event IDs supplied by the homeserver response, not on the requested pair
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1052 and 1284 later edit and reply lookups trust this cache

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The bot is a legitimate member of the room and the homeserver enforces history visibility, so anything the bot can read seems fair to bridge.
evidence: src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1288 fetch is made with getIntent() (the bridge bot), not with anything tied to event.sender
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1276-1318 no check anywhere that event.sender could see replyEventId (membership or history visibility)

conflicts.what: A strict 'sender must have been able to see the target' rule (T4) can break normal replies to older messages from users who joined later under shared history, and to events only in the cache. The same-room check for T1 must keep those replies quoting the original (MatrixHandler.ts:1284, 1316-1317).

fairness_risks: Replies to an event that cannot be fetched must still go to IRC as plain text (MatrixHandler.ts:1306-1312). A fix that drops the message, or throws in place of falling back, contradicts this existing behaviour (CWE-755 angle).
Edits in PM rooms fetch through the IRC ghost's intent (MatrixHandler.ts:1059-1062). A room check must use event.room_id there too, and must not require the bot to be in the PM room.
Cached same-room replies and edits (MatrixHandler.ts:1052, 1284) must keep producing quoted or diffed output without a refetch.
If T4 were tested, replies to messages sent before the replier joined are a legitimate shape under 'shared' history visibility, and a membership-at-time rule would refuse them.

design.why: Only two solid independent groups exist in-repo: the reply fetch (T1, with T3 closed by the same room check before line 1303) and the edit/diff fetch (T2). T2 is a good deepseek-type trap because the FIXME and the diff-only output give a strong reason to dismiss it. T4 is the only candidate with a mimo-type coupled value (legitimate replies to old messages), but it is inferred rather than tied to a published fix, and it is hard to test fairly. That gives fewer than 3 confidently independent traps with distinct reasons to dismiss, so the candidate is not usable as a 3-5 trap stack. As a 2-trap stack, T1+T2 works.

unverified: The exact content of fix A (4af7d3009f10) and fix B (1835e047f269) was not inspected (no git access in this run). The inference is that A adds a room_id equality check to the reply fetch (T1) and B covers the remaining route, most likely the edit fetch (T2) or a sender-visibility rule (T4). a_fix_leaves_b_open is left null for that reason. b_in_code_a_wrote=false is based on both fetch sites existing before A (MatrixHandler.ts:1067, 1288).
Whether the homeserver's /rooms/{roomId}/event/{eventId} endpoint returns events whose room_id differs from the path, which is the precondition for T1/T2 against a non-malicious bridge homeserver.
Whether T4 (sender visibility) is in scope of either advisory. CWE-280 suggests a permission-handling angle, but this is not confirmed.
No dependency-bump fix found. Both fetch sites are in-repo, but this was not checked against the advisory text.
